boot.when: Use when starting a session or a new slice of work: loads ranked past lessons, blockers, handoffs addressed to you and unread bus mail for that task.
keywords: what do i need to know

delta.when: Use when you come back after a break or mid-session and want only what changed since your last boot: lists moved areas and commits; --ack marks them seen.

compare.when: Use when you need what one set has that another lacks (files touched vs tracked, CLI vs MCP verbs, code terms vs lexicon): a checked set difference.

hand_rolled.why: compare refuses mismatched key types and flags an incompletely collected side instead of reporting false gaps

timeline.when: Use when asking what happened in what order, or why something broke recently: lines up events, git commits and task changes in one time-ordered column.

discover.when: Use when you wonder whether a command for something already exists: lists every verb with its purpose; --semantic asks by meaning instead of by word.

hand_rolled.why: discover lists every verb with its purpose and can search by meaning

learn.when: Use when you found a reusable fix, gotcha or failed approach another agent could act on: records a lesson; --repeat-of notes an old lesson broken again.
learn.args: <you> --experiment SHORT_NAME --tried "what did not work" --result "what happened" --recommend "Use when ..." --success yes

scope.when: Use when a lesson seems too narrow or too broad for where it applies: shows or sets its scope, widens it on cross-harness evidence; set and widen change the lesson.

wish.when: Use when a tool or workflow annoys you or is missing something: files a numbered ergonomics wish in the wishlist so it gets curated, safe against concurrent writers.

hand_rolled.why: wish numbers the entry and locks the file so concurrent filings are not lost

wish-curate.when: Use when clearing the wishlist backlog: bare lists the oldest open wishes; with --id it folds, keeps or declines one and rewrites docs/WISHLIST.md.

hand_rolled.why: wish-curate takes the wishlist lock; a hand edit can lose a concurrent filing or tear the file

web.when: Use when you need a web page or a web search: fetches a URL with caching, receipts and paging (no silent truncation, PDFs handled) or runs a search; content is untrusted.

hand_rolled.why: web caches, pages long text instead of truncating, records a receipt and fences the content as untrusted

ask.when: Use when you want another model's answer or second opinion on one question: calls a helper model once; can fan out lenses, run in background, or ask a live seat.

hand_rolled.why: ask handles keys, continuation of cut answers, and journals the route

discord.when: Use when the human wants fleet updates on their phone: status shows the outbound Discord webhook setup; test and send post real messages to the channel.

hand_rolled.why: discord reads the configured webhook without printing it and keeps the forwarding rules in one place

gateway.when: Use when Discord messages from the operator are not reaching the fleet: status shows the inbound Discord gateway; restart kills and relaunches it, changing live state.

hand_rolled.why: gateway finds the live process reliably and restart relaunches it detached with its log, never leaving it dead

sift.when: Use when a question needs more reading than one context holds, e.g. does a term mean two things in the code: fans readers over evidence, reports disagreement first.

friction.when: Use when asking how well a seat's asks get answered: read-only report of open, answered and dead asks, dead rate and time to settle over the last week.

report.when: Use when you want to present findings as a visual HTML report: prints a page scaffold with the house design kit inlined, ready to fill and publish.

resident.when: Use when naming, showing or placing a long-lived agent identity: manages resident callsigns and adjudicates their verdicts; ratify is human-only and writes.

scout.when: Use when about to start work and unsure if a seat is already on it or it was done: a resident model reads ledger and locks, answers, and files a verdict.

doc.when: Use when writing a design, brief, report or ruling that belongs in the docs library: creates it with the header, name and home, or adopts an existing loose markdown file.

hand_rolled.why: doc new stamps the header contract, canonical name and library home that a hand-written file lacks

tag-anti-pattern.when: Use when an existing lesson describes something that turned out to be a known-bad approach: tags it as a reusable anti-pattern so recall warns against it; writes memory.

corpus.when: Use when building the replay eval set from past tasks: archive transcripts, mine candidate scenarios, list or validate; accept, reject and retire change it.

replay.when: Use when testing whether a harness config change helps: re-runs a recorded scenario against a candidate config in an isolated sandbox, never the live store or bus.

grade.when: Use when evaluating a harness change on test scenarios: grades runs, compares two candidates, estimates noise and statistical power, or labels judge calibration.

review.when: Use when a harness change awaits human sign-off: list and show queued candidates, record a decision, apply or roll back; apply edits the live harness config.

loop.when: Use when running or inspecting the automated harness-improvement loop: proposes, runs and grades candidate configs; run spends real money under a required daily cap.

memreplay.when: Use when you want proof that a specific lesson actually changes outcomes: snapshots memory, replays scenarios with and without the lesson; run and drain spend money.

precompile.when: Use when turning proven lessons into guards, skills, subagents or instruction lines: plan shows where each lesson routes, build compiles a candidate, check tests a tree.
keywords: make a guard from a lesson

modes.when: Use when deciding whether lessons should be shown at action time or baked into skills and hooks: shows the memory mode, compares modes, flags stale compiled lessons.

compress.when: Use when trimming what the harness injects into context: lists the pieces, reads their usage telemetry, and searches for which pieces matter; run spends task runs.

provenance.when: Use when you need to know which harness, model, effort and environment a session runs under: shows the session's provenance record, writing it if missing.

recall.when: Use when you hit a problem someone may have seen before, or before trying a fix: searches past lessons by keyword; --full pulls one lesson's whole record.

hand_rolled.why: recall ranks and renders lessons from the store and its file mirror instead of raw keys

list.when: Use when you want to browse every lesson in shared memory rather than search it: prints lessons newest first with a total count.

recall-at.when: Use when about to edit a file or run a command: shows the lessons and peer locks that apply to it; the hook usually does this for you automatically.

recall-feedback.when: Use when a recalled lesson actually changed what you did, or was off-target: votes it useful or noise so future recall ranks it better; writes to shared memory.

repeat.when: Use when someone repeated a mistake a lesson already warned about: records the violation and whether recall fired; --report shows how long after learning each one broke.

recall-prevention.when: Use when asking whether recalled lessons actually prevented failures: read-only report of violations and prevention candidates from the outcome stage log.

recall-curate.when: Use when recall keeps surfacing lessons that never help: reports lessons to bench and stale counters to prune; --apply changes shared memory.

audit.when: Use when you suspect documented beliefs have drifted from reality, such as the verb registry versus the actual parser: prints match or drift rows, read-only.

injections.when: Use when asking what recall pushed into agents' contexts and what it cost: lists recently injected lessons, their targets and token totals (default 24 hours).

harnesses.when: Use when asking what your harness (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, bare CLI) actually supports here, like hooks or automatic recall: prints the capability matrix.

hooks.when: Use when recall injections or other harness hooks are missing, noisy or need switching: shows hook wiring and installs, removes, enables or disables it; edits settings.

hand_rolled.why: hooks install/uninstall edits settings safely and can dry-run

link.when: Use when connecting this fleet to another fleet: identity, invites, joining, membership, sync and cross-fleet mail; invites, joins and removals change shared state.

setup.when: Use when setting Aurora up on a new machine or for a new harness: wires hooks, agent id, MCP and git hooks; writes config, so try --dry-run first.

fleet.when: Use when you want a local Ollama model: lists the local model roster, picks one for a capability and memory budget, or calls one once with a prompt.

hand_rolled.why: fleet knows the roster, capabilities and VRAM limits and routes to the right model

triage.when: Use when reviewing which lessons earn their keep: read-only ranking into protect, cost-with-no-return and noise, for a human to merge, graduate or retire.

recall-counters.when: Use when lesson usefulness counts look split or orphaned: reports misnamed and orphan usage counters; --fold merges and prunes them in shared memory.

hand_rolled.why: recall-counters knows which counters are canonical and keeps the ones that carry credit

graduate.when: Use when a lesson's rule is now enforced by automation such as a hook or test: retires it from recall so it stops taking space; --undo brings it back; writes memory.

sha.when: Use when a commit SHA cited in a doc, lesson or ticket is not found in git: follows it across this repo's history rewrites to the commit it became.

note.when: Use when a project decision or fact should outlive the session (not a lesson): records a durable note; re-noting the same title updates it, --get reads one.

notes.when: Use when you want the current project notes (decisions, state, conventions) rather than lessons: lists active notes; --project regenerates the memory digest file.

hand_rolled.why: notes reads the live store; the digest file can be stale

wrap.when: Use when ending a session or handing off: drafts a where-we-are note from this session's commits, lessons and notes; previews by default, --commit records it.

status.when: Use when asking whether shared memory is up and healthy: shows the storage backend, lesson and key counts, and whether logging paths are silently degraded.

hand_rolled.why: status also reports the fallback mirror, counts and narrative health, not just a ping

stats.when: Use when asking whether recall is paying off: shows how often lessons surfaced, helped, changed an outcome, and were captured, over hours or a per-day trend.

log.when: Use when something happened worth keeping on the timeline but is not a reusable lesson: records a narrative beat (session, note, commit) plus a raw event.

episode.when: Use when bookending a session: shows the current open episode, closes it with a drafted summary, or accepts that summary; close and accept write the record.

task.when: Use when proposing, claiming, finishing or listing shared work items, or asking what to do next: manages the task ledger lifecycle; most subcommands change shared state.

story.when: Use when asking for the project's narrative or what was happening at a given time: prints its chapters and themes; --mark starts a new named chapter.

handoff.when: Use when you stop, switch agents or end the day with work unfinished: writes a briefing the next agent's boot shows automatically; --list reads ones addressed to you.
keywords: pick up where i left off

events.when: Use when you need the raw history of what agents did (tool calls, commands, messages): search, view events around a time or beat, or fetch one; --capture writes.

roster.when: Use when asking which agent seats are actually alive and working right now: lists each seat's proven liveness; --reap re-homes mail stranded on dead seats.

season-score.when: Use when scoring a round of the agents' bounty season or comparing its two rule sets on the same claims: prints scores, ranks and the policy delta, read-only.

grant.when: Use when a seat needs a capability or role changed: mints, revokes or lists access grants with a reason and time box; admins only, and it changes shared access.

hand_rolled.why: grant writes atomically, validates the schema, records a reason and time box, and can be undone with --revoke

doctor.when: Use when the fleet seems stuck or slow, or after deploying to a machine: grades each agent's progress (wedged, stalled, frozen) and services; --deploy checks a machine.

hand_rolled.why: doctor judges progress, not mere process presence, and reports services alongside

promoted.when: Use when looking for past handoffs, decisions or important bus messages that must not be lost: lists durable salient messages and flags ones nobody handled.
keywords: what was decided on the bus

lookback.when: Use when asking why something is the way it is: searches docs, research, notes, promoted messages, chapters and git commit bodies for the rationale, layered.
lookback.args: "why does boot use a token budget"

knowledge-map.when: Use when exploring what the house knows about a topic beyond a flat search: shows matching lessons, notes and docs, their linked neighbours and retired records.

fence.when: Use when a decision needs two independent passes plus a reconciliation: opens a workspace with brief and pass slots and checks method rules at seal; writes files.

hand_rolled.why: fence open creates the slots with tool-derived paths and runs the method checks at seal time

flow.when: Use when a message seems lost, unanswered or delivered twice: shows recent bus asks and answers as a waterfall with gaps and duplicate copies, read-only.

packet-trace.when: Use when wondering which lane a bus message kind would be routed to: explains the static routing rule for one kind without sending anything.

packet-stats.when: Use when checking how the bus router is classifying and routing message kinds before trusting a routing change: reads its per-kind decision counters.

mailbox.when: Use when you need one bus message's full state or to declare act/decline/defer on it: shows body, readers and intent; --retire-ghosts --apply writes declines.

bifrost-ack.when: Use when you have handled a bus message addressed to you: records durably that you acted on it (reading alone does not); only the addressee can ack.

console-log.when: Use when asking what the operator did from the console, such as interjections, bus pauses and resumes, or dropped files: lists those durable events.

bifrost-sync.when: Use when starting a turn or when someone may have messaged you: shows presence and unread bus mail without consuming it; --consume marks it read.

hand_rolled.why: bifrost-sync renders unread mail per agent and tracks presence and cursors correctly

bifrost-standby.when: Use when ending a turn and you should wake on new mail: drains the inbox, reports, then blocks as the wake listener; run it as a background task.

hand_rolled.why: bifrost-standby names the work lane and parents the listener so its exit actually re-invokes the harness

forecast.when: Use when making a falsifiable prediction about a change at a gate, or scoring one at review: registers bets, scores them, shows calibration; register and score write.

bifrost-send.when: Use when you need to tell, ask or answer another agent: sends a message on the bus; use --text-file for long or flag-like bodies; directed asks arm a reply deadline.

hand_rolled.why: bifrost-send stamps sender, kind and reply links that raw stream writes lack

suite-baseline.when: Use when the test suite shows failures and you must know which are yours: records or diffs the suite receipt; --whose runs tests and attributes each failure.

hand_rolled.why: suite-baseline --whose attributes failures without stash-bisecting a shared worktree
after a full-suite run, record it with suite-baseline --from-file so the next seat diffs instead of re-classifying

bifrost-drain.when: Use when a bus runner must be restarted without losing in-flight work: asks it to finish its current message, release its lock and exit; changes runner state.

hand_rolled.why: drain lets the runner finish its message and release its lock instead of being killed mid-turn

bifrost-pause.when: Use when the human must barge in and the whole fleet should stop: freezes every bus auto-responder, changing shared state (--soft lets work finish); set --ttl.

bifrost-resume.when: Use when the bus was paused and seats should pick up work again: unfreezes the bus auto-responders; changes shared state for the whole fleet.

bifrost-skip-to-now.when: Use when an agent is stuck replaying an old message backlog and the bus is already paused: jumps its cursors to now, dropping unread mail; audited, changes shared state.

hand_rolled.why: skip-to-now is audited, requires a pause, and moves all cursors consistently

bifrost-nudge.when: Use when one specific peer must look at something now or adjust course: sends a targeted interrupt, steer or inform signal; interrupt drops its current work.

seat-identity.when: Use when hooks, locks or the roster call you by the wrong agent name: shows or binds this session's seat id, which beats the shared environment variable.

hand_rolled.why: a running session cannot change its own env; the per-session binding is what hooks actually read

lock.when: Use when you are about to edit a shared file while other agents are live: claims an advisory lock on the path so others see it; unlock when done.

unlock.when: Use when you finish editing a path you locked: releases your advisory lock so peers can edit it; you cannot release another seat's lock.

focus.when: Use when starting or finishing work on a specific ledger task: checks this session in so tool calls and cost are attributed to it; --clear checks out.

locks.when: Use when about to edit a shared file while other agents are live, or asking who is editing what: lists held advisory path locks with holder and age.
keywords: is anyone working on this file

bifrost-fetch.when: Use when a bus message was clipped or says its payload spilled to a blob ref: fetches the full stored body by its ref.

captions.when: Use when a YouTube link comes up and you need what is said in it: downloads the captions only (never video) and writes clean readable text.

hand_rolled.why: captions skips the video download and cleans and punctuates the text
the script is the implementation; the captions verb is the door other seats will find

reply.when: Use when answering the human operator over the bus or Discord: sends your reply in one argument and says honestly whether delivery failed; sends a message.

boop.when: Use when you just want to confirm the command door answers at all, or a quick look at what is going on around you with --surface: always replies, changes nothing.

find.when: Use when you need a file by name anywhere on the machine, including outside the repo: indexed whole-disk search (Everything on Windows, plocate elsewhere).

hand_rolled.why: find uses a machine-wide index and ranks results instead of walking the whole disk
find wraps the index with presets, ranking and a clear message when the indexer is missing

manual.when: Use when a design or platform question needs reference manuals such as Apple HIG or One UI: searches the shelved manuals and returns labelled passages.

shell-home.when: Use when your shell keeps landing in the wrong directory after a session event: shows where fresh harness shells start; --set picks a home and edits your bashrc.

sweep.when: Use when starting a turn or getting your bearings: one read-only snapshot of your bus mail, parked asks, fleet health and what moved recently.

orient.when: Use when you are lost or returning after a break and want one view of where you stand: composes awareness, a focus on a verb, seat or thread, and landmarks.

shadow.when: Use when you want to preview what a bus or toolbox action would do, whether you may do it and what it costs, before doing it: renders it without executing.

college.when: Use when learning a topic rigorously with separate seats: records sources, a sealed lecture, an independent claim audit, teach-backs and errata; it calls no model.

ground.when: Use when unsure a verb really exists, is wired and is permitted for you, or recovering a seat's state after lost context: prints the evidence ladder; read-only.

eye.when: Use when searching what was said in past agent sessions or what the operator asked for before: indexes session transcripts and finds, cites, counts or traces utterances.

hand_rolled.why: eye indexes every session, labels speakers and returns citable addresses

capture.when: Use when a bus message looks truncated or you need its exact text: reads the full message by stream id or a sender's latest, optionally saving it verbatim.

hand_rolled.why: capture reads both inbox streams, unwraps the payload and can persist it verbatim

alias.when: Use when you keep typing the same sequence of verbs: mints, lists or retires a named composition on your toolbelt; mint and retire change shared state.

run.when: Use when you have saved a personal command alias or macro and want to run it: expands the alias into its CLI steps and runs them; --dry shows the steps only.

bench.when: Use when stale asks clog your inbox: lists, parks or unparks messages so fresh mail flows; parked mail is kept and its sender notified, so park changes shared state.

tool.when: Use when trying out a draft play script an agent wrote: lists the sandboxed play tools or runs one with time limits and a receipt.

hand_rolled.why: tool run executes the draft inside the sandbox with a timeout and records a receipt

kata.when: Use when you have authored or changed a toolbelt alias and want to know if it is real: checks each step parses against the CLI and raises its trust level.

toast.when: Use when a peer's lesson saved you time: sends them thanks tied to that lesson, verified against the lesson store; sends a bus message.

clobber-scan.when: Use when reviewing a Python file or diff that writes shared control keys: flags unconditional overwrites that could clobber another agent's state, to confirm.

tally.when: Use when several independent reviewers answered the same research opening and you want consensus: aligns their answers by question and shows agree or conflict.

pulse.when: Use when asking where work is piling up across the fleet: read-only pressure map of each seat's backlog, sorted into critical, elevated and normal zones.

reentry.when: Use when the human operator returns and asks what they missed: renders what moved since their last word and their one open question, quoted verbatim.

glance.when: Use when you want a bounded snapshot of the task program: what needs attention, open tasks, and which checks cannot be made, read-only.

secret.when: Use when the human needs to give you an API key or password: opens a paste window that saves it to the vault, never the transcript; bare lists which exist.

hand_rolled.why: secret takes the value through a window or stdin so it never lands in a transcript or shell history

flightdeck.when: Use when you want the whole fleet on one page: combines agent health, pressure, lane health, locks and recent commits; --agent drills into one seat.

stand-down.when: Use when this session is retiring and a successor must take your agent's seat: permanently yields the seat for this session, no reclaim; changes shared seat state.

unwedge.when: Use when an agent seems stuck, silent or not answering: read-only diagnosis combining runner, lanes, backlog and locks into a verdict and recommended fix.

hand_rolled.why: unwedge reads runner, lane cursor, depths and locks together and says what to do

followup.when: Use when a verdict or report leaves a question its author must answer: appends the question to its open questions and queues it for that seat; writes both.

defer.when: Use when you need a command run that your seat lacks permission for (exec, write, network): queues it for a capable seat; --done with a receipt discharges it.

watch.when: Use when starting a long run that must not die silently: declares it so silence raises an alarm, checkpoints while alive, and stands down when done.

kit.when: Use when a seat needs the standard recovery shortcuts for wake loops and stalls: --show previews the kit; without it, installs the bundle onto that seat's toolbelt.
